newsitem.title: USA: Clinton says NATO-Russia deal "an historic step".
newsitem.headline: Clinton says NATO-Russia deal "an historic step".

text.p: President Bill Clinton on Wednesday welcomed the NATO-Russia agreement on a new peaceful relationship as "an historic step closer to a peaceful, undivided, democratic Europe."

Clinton told reporters a deal reached in Moscow earlier on Wednesday opened the way to the signing in Paris later this month of a new framework for Russia-NATO relations. It was drawn up partly to assuage Russian concerns over the western alliance's expansion to the east.

"Today in Moscow we have taken an historic step closer to a peaceful, undivided, democratic Europe for the first time in history," Clinton told reporters at the White House in response to the deal worked out in Moscow between NATO and Russian negotiators.
"Russia will work closely with NATO but not in NATO, giving Russia a voice in but not a veto over NATO's business," he said.

Russia strongly opposes the expansion of the western alliance, its Cold War enemy, into former communist states once allied with Moscow. But with NATO planning to go ahead and name new members in July, Moscow has sought an agreement that goes as far as possible to protect its interests.

Clinton said under the deal reached in Moscow it was made clear that NATO's mission "is not to threaten, confine or in any way undermine Russia." He added: "What the language does is to make it clear that there are no plans, and there are no reasons to in effect activate old Warsaw pact military installations for what you might call traditional NATO aggressive forward posturing."
